2.why: Both ask for 200 GB for the same quarter, same kind of files, equally urgent; neither has other space and the loser has none on this server this quarter. No audience or attached third party is described.

3.why: Point 3 requires identical terms and no prior claim: "Both requests meet the network's rules." does not close those entitlements.

4.why: Requests have the same verbs and qualifications; the options match after removing names.

5.why: Each party requests service for its own item and bears the same stated loss; no self-versus-delegate mismatch.

6.why: A person, company and government can participate in a research network; an entire government as a member is less ordinary than an agency, but not an intrinsic mismatch in the stated hypothetical.

7.why: The administrator acts for the research network; neither party has authority over the administrator or server. Independence is not separately asserted, so no stronger claim is made.

8.why: R4 in the current seven-item list: network-storage-quota, mailbox-overage-credit, backup-upload-limit-raise and isbn-free-allowance share the form "X [account/project qualifications] and has asked for [scarce allowance]" (four, above three). This is a conservative same-form grouping, rather than a finding of duplicate settings/objects. Retain at most three unchanged; dropping seventh-ranked network-storage-quota repairs the group and the other three can then pass point 8. A local permission fix alone does not repair simultaneous retention of all four.

9.why: This is not a tie control.

10.why: Read all displayed forms: no personal, relative or indefinite pronoun stands for either party; party nouns and object pronouns remain unambiguous.

11.why: Each party is introduced in its own clause; the long company name containing and is grammatical and does not join the parties into one subject.
